text:
ConocoPhillips gained slightly today, but the stock has lost nearly 10% over the past two weeks—a decline that started right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The timing suggests the earnings report itself disappointed investors, or forward guidance was weaker than expected, overriding any day-to-day market moves. Meanwhile, oil prices have softened: U.S. crude is trading at $99.64 per barrel, down from levels that likely prevailed when the stock was near $154 two weeks ago, and that drop in crude value directly pressures energy companies' profitability and investor appetite for their shares.

The broader election results—a Democratic sweep and setback for the Trump administration—are adding headwinds for oil stocks. Investors are now bracing for renewable energy policies to gain ground and less political support for fossil fuel expansion, which could weigh on long-term demand expectations and investor sentiment toward traditional energy companies, even as geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain elevated.
